# @mission-platform/i18n

Framework-agnostic [i18next](https://www.i18next.com/) integration for Mission Platform.

## Entry points

| Import | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `@mission-platform/i18n` | Framework-neutral core. `createForgeI18N(options)` builds a configured i18next instance; also exports `forgeNamespace`, `localeNamespaces`, `mergeLocales`, `deepMergeMessages`/`deepMergeLocales`, `FORGE_DEFAULT_NAMESPACE`, `FORGE_NAMESPACE_PREFIX`, the `ForgeI18N` instance type, and the `Mp*` message types. |
| `@mission-platform/i18n/vue` | Vue 3 adapter (built on `i18next-vue`). `createForgeI18NVue(i18n)` returns a Vue plugin; `useI18n(namespace?)` returns `{ t, i18next, locale, setLocale }`. |
| `@mission-platform/i18n/react` | React adapter (built on `react-i18next`). `ForgeI18NProvider` supplies the instance; `useI18n(namespace?)` returns `{ t, i18n, locale, setLocale }`. |

## Usage

`createForgeI18N` returns a plain, synchronously-initialised i18next instance.
Interpolation uses single-brace delimiters (`{name}`) and HTML escaping is left
to the framework (`escapeValue: false`). Nested (`nav.notes`) and array-indexed
(`items.0.title`) keys resolve out of the box. With no `namespace`, messages are
registered under the default `translation` namespace.

## Namespaces (`mp.<workspace>`)

Strings are grouped into i18next namespaces: every package lives under
`mp.<package_name>` and every app under `mp.<app_name>`. Build a namespace name
with `forgeNamespace('<workspace>')` (e.g. `forgeNamespace('breakpoints')` →
`'mp.breakpoints'`).

- Apps pass their own `namespace: forgeNamespace('<app>')` as the default and the
  per-namespace bundles via `namespaces` (use `localeNamespaces(locale, bundles)`
  to turn the extractor's namespace-keyed runtime `src/locales/<locale>.yaml`
  into the expected shape). The default namespace falls back to every other
  namespace, so component code keeps resolving the keys it owns.
- Package components resolve their own namespace explicitly with
  `useI18n(forgeNamespace('<package>'))`.
- Apps override any package/component strings per namespace via `overrides`,
  which is deep-merged on top of the package's own bundle (only the listed keys
  change).

```ts
import { createForgeI18N, localeNamespaces, forgeNamespace } from '@mission-platform/i18n'

// `enBundles` is the parsed, namespace-keyed `src/locales/en.yaml`.
const i18n = createForgeI18N({
  namespace: forgeNamespace('my-care-notes'),
  namespaces: localeNamespaces('en', enBundles),
  overrides: {
    // Relabel one breakpoints-package string without touching the rest.
    [forgeNamespace('breakpoints')]: { en: { breakpoint: 'Viewport:' } },
  },
})
```

### Vue 3

```ts
// main.ts
import { createForgeI18N } from '@mission-platform/i18n'
import { createForgeI18NVue } from '@mission-platform/i18n/vue'

const i18n = createForgeI18N({ messages: { en: { hello: 'Hello {name}' } } })
app.use(createForgeI18NVue(i18n))
```

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useI18n } from '@mission-platform/i18n/vue'
const { t, locale, setLocale } = useI18n()
</script>

<template>
  <button>{{ t('hello', { name: 'World' }) }}</button>
</template>
```

### React

```tsx
import { createForgeI18N } from '@mission-platform/i18n'
import { ForgeI18NProvider, useI18n } from '@mission-platform/i18n/react'

const i18n = createForgeI18N({ messages: { en: { hello: 'Hello {name}' } } })

function Greeting() {
  const { t } = useI18n()
  return <button>{t('hello', { name: 'World' })}</button>
}

root.render(
  <ForgeI18NProvider i18n={i18n}>
    <Greeting />
  </ForgeI18NProvider>,
)
```
